assumptions.statement: All node and state sets are finite and nonempty, the graph is acyclic, and every local kernel is normalized with respect to counting measure.
A hard intervention replaces each selected local kernel by the corresponding point mass and leaves every other mechanism unchanged.
Every passive or intervened response is compared as the complete retained joint mass table on the ordered boundary (R,O), without conditioning on null events.
The only admitted boundary state relabelings in the binary witness are the four independent bit flips on R and O.
The finite typed category is a declared mathematical model class, not an ontologically canonical description.
Any identification of informational quantities, agents, geometry, or units with physical ontology requires an additional operational bridge not supplied by this theorem.

claims.statement: For every two admissible finite reduced typed-intervention experiments in the declared binary-symmetric-channel subcategory, equality of their passive retained (R,O) law implies isomorphism of their reduced protocol-indexed retained response experiments.
claims.quantifiers: For all reduced experiments Red(P) and Red(Q) arising from admissible finite binary-symmetric-channel presentations P and Q with retained nodes (R,O), if Ubar_pass(Red(P)) and Ubar_pass(Red(Q)) have the same complete passive retained joint law up to an admitted typed boundary relabeling, then Red(P) and Red(Q) are isomorphic as reduced intervention experiments by an identity-preserving protocol-monoid isomorphism intertwining every retained response law up to one admitted typed boundary relabeling.
claims.falsifier: Construct an identity-preserving protocol-monoid isomorphism intertwining the two witness response maps under one admitted typed boundary relabeling, or show either witness is outside the frozen domain.
scope_limits: Declared finite BSC subcategory only.
No category-independent, ontological, autonomous-agency, continuum, gauge, or physical-identification conclusion.

claims.statement: Finite normalized typed DAG presentations with all partial hard interventions and typed invertible transport form the declared raw groupoid, and every observational or intervened law is normalized.
claims.quantifiers: For every object and typed isomorphism satisfying the frozen finite-domain assumptions.
claims.falsifier: Exhibit a normalized finite DAG object whose truncated product is not normalized or a typed isomorphism that fails to transport an intervention response.
scope_limits: Finite hard-intervention category only.

claims.statement: All partial hard assignments on a presentation form a monoid under total right override, with the empty assignment as identity.
claims.quantifiers: For every finite presentation P and all contexts i,j,k in A_P.
claims.falsifier: Find a node and three valid contexts for which the two parenthesizations select different final assignments.
scope_limits: Partial hard assignments only.

claims.statement: Equality of complete two-sided retained-response signatures is an equivalence relation and a two-sided congruence on the right-override context monoid.
claims.quantifiers: For every finite presentation P and all contexts i,j,a,b,u,v in A_P.
claims.falsifier: Find equivalent contexts separated by multiplication on the left or right.
scope_limits: Equivalence is defined by the complete two-sided signature, not identity response alone.

claims.statement: The behavioral quotient has well-defined multiplication, identity, and descended retained response, and typed raw isomorphisms define a functor Red from raw presentations to reduced intervention experiments.
claims.quantifiers: For every declared raw object P and every typed raw isomorphism g.
claims.falsifier: Find equivalent representatives with different quotient products or responses, or a raw isomorphism that does not preserve behavioral classes.
scope_limits: Declared finite groupoids and typed boundary relabelings.

claims.statement: The admitted same-signature chains L(1/4,1/3) and L(1/3,1/4) have the identical complete passive retained law (7/24,5/24,5/24,7/24).
claims.quantifiers: For the two explicitly declared BSC objects L_1 and L_2.
claims.falsifier: Compute unequal composed crossovers or unequal atoms in the complete passive retained tables.
scope_limits: Exact rational BSC pair only.

claims.statement: Each same-signature witness has exactly fifteen two-sided behavioral classes: nine singleton classes with O unassigned and six size-three classes in which a hard assignment to O masks E.
claims.quantifiers: For every one of the twenty-seven partial contexts on R,E,O in each of L_1 and L_2.
claims.falsifier: Find an omitted raw context, two displayed classes with equal complete signatures, or one size-three class split by a contextual response.
scope_limits: Frozen binary chains and hard contexts only.

claims.statement: The L_1 response (1/3,1/6,1/3,1/6) is absent from the complete L_2 reduced response image under every one of the four admitted typed binary boundary relabelings.
claims.quantifiers: For every class of Red(L_2) and every independent binary state flip on R and O.
claims.falsifier: Exhibit an L_2 response class and admitted boundary flip whose relabeled law equals the unmatched L_1 response.
scope_limits: Complete response-image invariant; diagnostic total variation is not used.

claims.statement: Red(L_1) and Red(L_2) are nonisomorphic as identity-preserving response-intertwining reduced intervention experiments.
claims.quantifiers: For every identity-preserving protocol-monoid isomorphism candidate and every admitted typed boundary relabeling.
claims.falsifier: Construct an identity-preserving monoid isomorphism and one admitted boundary relabeling that intertwine every retained response.
scope_limits: Nonisomorphism in the declared FinRIE groupoid.

claims.statement: Forgetting an independent isolated binary node induces an identity-, multiplication-, and response-preserving isomorphism between the null extension and split reduced experiment.
claims.quantifiers: For both assignments to N, every one of the twenty-seven contexts on R,E,O, and every pair of left and right contexts.
claims.falsifier: Find a retained response depending on the isolated node or show that forgetting N fails to preserve or reflect behavioral equivalence.
scope_limits: Independent isolated node only.
Non-load-bearing control outside target ancestry.

claims.statement: The direct, split, and independent-null controls have the same nine retained-boundary intervention laws at the frozen parameters.
claims.quantifiers: For every partial assignment on the shared retained boundary R,O.
claims.falsifier: Exhibit one of the nine shared boundary contexts with unequal retained laws.
scope_limits: Shared-boundary control only; auxiliary interventions differ.

claims.statement: The bound exact implementation satisfies the frozen focused executable contract, and every one of nine specified semantic mutants is killed before exact source restoration.
claims.quantifiers: For the exact source, frozen test snapshot, RED and GREEN records, and nine mutation records contained in this package.
claims.falsifier: Reproduce a failing focused GREEN test, a surviving specified mutant, or a digest mismatch in the contained source and records.
scope_limits: Mechanical corroboration only; it does not prove mathematical nonisomorphism.

claims.statement: The reduced passive functor Ubar_pass is not essentially injective on the declared BSC subcategory.
claims.quantifiers: There exist two nonisomorphic reduced experiments X and Y with equal passive images.
claims.falsifier: Show that the equal-passive witness objects are isomorphic in the declared reduced groupoid.
scope_limits: Downstream corollary outside target ancestry.

claims.statement: No functor R from passive retained objects to reduced experiments can satisfy a natural isomorphism R Ubar_pass ~= identity on every reduced experiment in the declared BSC subcategory.
claims.quantifiers: For every proposed reconstruction functor R and natural isomorphism of the stated type.
claims.falsifier: Construct a functor and natural isomorphism R Ubar_pass ~= identity on the declared subcategory.
scope_limits: Does not rule out Ubar_pass R ~= identity.

claims.statement: The certified contradiction for R Ubar_pass ~= identity does not imply nonexistence of a conventional representative-selecting section satisfying Ubar_pass R ~= identity.
claims.quantifiers: For the logical content of the same-fiber contradiction and the two opposite functor-composition types.
claims.falsifier: Derive nonexistence of Ubar_pass R ~= identity using only the certified same-fiber pair and without additional assumptions.
scope_limits: No existence or canonical-choice theorem for such a section is asserted.

claims.statement: The declared finite typed-intervention category is the ontologically canonical category of agents or physical systems.
claims.quantifiers: Across all admissible ontological and operational representations.
claims.falsifier: Produce a competing operationally adequate category not equivalent under a justified ontology criterion.
scope_limits: Explicitly outside the frozen target.
open_obligations: Define an ontology criterion and prove a scope-matched uniqueness or equivalence theorem.

claims.statement: A mediator, intervention target, or reduced protocol class in the finite model is thereby an autonomous agent.
claims.quantifiers: For every modeled mediator, target, or protocol class.
claims.falsifier: Give an admitted modeled variable that lacks the proposed operational criteria for autonomous agency.
scope_limits: Explicitly outside the frozen target.
open_obligations: Define autonomous agency operationally and establish the required bridge for modeled variables.

claims.statement: Every passive object in a justified ambient category has a unique minimal reduced intervention realization up to the intended equivalence.
claims.quantifiers: For every passive object in a future explicitly declared ambient category.
claims.falsifier: Exhibit nonunique minimal objects under the proposed criterion.
scope_limits: Future work; no ambient category or minimality criterion is presently frozen.
open_obligations: Define the ambient category, minimality criterion, and equivalence.
Prove existence and uniqueness or provide a scope-matched obstruction.

claims.statement: The same reduction and nonidentifiability theorem extends unchanged to arbitrary soft, stochastic, or continuous interventions.
claims.quantifiers: For every such intervention family in a future declared category.
claims.falsifier: Find a well-typed soft or continuous intervention family for which composition or behavioral quotienting fails.
scope_limits: Hard finite interventions only are certified.
open_obligations: Define the richer intervention algebra, equivalence, topology, and continuity or measurability conditions.

claims.statement: The finite theorem extends to continuum, bundle, gauge, or renormalization-scale categories with all overlap, covariance, and closure conditions.
claims.quantifiers: For all objects and morphisms in a future explicitly typed continuum or gauge category.
claims.falsifier: Exhibit a topology, overlap, gauge, singular-stratum, or coarse-graining obstruction to the proposed extension.
scope_limits: Finite discrete theorem only.
open_obligations: Define the continuum or gauge category and intervention action.
Prove global coherence, covariance, quotient regularity, and any renormalization closure.

claims.statement: Informational responses or updates in the finite sections thereby determine physical geometry, constants, units, time, or other physical properties.
claims.quantifiers: For every proposed informational-to-physical identification.
claims.falsifier: Produce operationally distinguishable physical systems with the same proposed informational invariant or a dimensional inconsistency in the identification.
scope_limits: No physical identification is part of the frozen theorem.
open_obligations: Specify dimensions, units, observables, and an operational bridge.
Establish the required continuum, gauge, and empirical evidence.
